candidate.answerReason: The daily pay equals Tony's age in completed years. His earnings bound his ending age N by 12.6 ≤ N ≤ 13.6, so N = 13.

methods.label: Bound the daily pay
methods.explanation:
Working two hours makes Tony's daily pay numerically equal to his age in completed years: at age \(n\), he earns \(2(0.50)n=n\) dollars per working day.

Let \(N\) be his age in completed years at the end of the period. In six months he can have at most one birthday, so his age on each working day was either \(N-1\) or \(N\). Therefore his earnings satisfy
\[
50(N-1)\le 630\le 50N.
\]
Dividing by \(50\) and rearranging gives
\[
12.6\le N\le 13.6.
\]
Since \(N\) is an integer, \(N=13\). These earnings are possible: \(20\) days at \(12\) dollars and \(30\) days at \(13\) dollars give \(20(12)+30(13)=630\). Tony was \(13\) years old at the end, choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
